::: {#def-reference-level}
#### Reference level

The **reference level** of a categorical variable
is the category that does not have its own
[indicator variable](#def-indicator-variable).
An observation in the reference level has the value 0
for every indicator variable of that categorical variable.

:::

::: notes
For example, take chromosomal sex $S$ with the indicator variable $M$
for "male".
The category "female" has no indicator variable,
so "female" is the reference level, and a female newborn has $M = 0$.
In @exr-dummy-coding,
category A1 of `behpat` is the reference level.

The choice of a reference level is arbitrary
and does not limit what we can do with the resulting model.
It only makes it more computationally convenient
to make inferences about comparisons involving that reference group.
In the example, we could instead use "male" as the reference level
and the indicator variable $F$ for "female".
Both choices describe the same two groups.
:::
